title: Fill support messages with the customer's own data

blocks.text: The support team writes message templates such as `Hello {customer}, ticket {ticket} is closed.` and the help desk fills them with each customer's data. The team picks the names, and some have dots in them, such as `{invoice.no}`. Since refunds were added, some messages fail to send, and one went out with a file path that had lost its backslashes.

items: `render(values)`: the template with every value of the map filled in;
`fill(text, name, value)`: `text` with `value` in place of `{name}`.

blocks.text: When you're done, every value appears exactly as the customer's data holds it, wherever its name appears, and no other text changes. About four lines in total.

cases.says: each {name} in the template is replaced by its value
a {name} with no value is left in the text as it is
a value holding $ or \ appears in the message exactly as given
a name with a dot replaces only that exact name, not a similar one with another character there
a name that appears twice in the template is filled in both places

origin.section: replace() Replaces Every Literal Match; replaceAll() Interprets Both of Its Arguments

concepts: replace() replaces every occurrence of literal text, while replaceAll() reads its first argument as a regex and its replacement's $ and \ as syntax.
